key_insight: An agentic LLM system can query TCGA clinical data in natural language, choose the right analysis tools, and deliver accurate, auditable answers.
clinical_relevance: This could make large oncology clinical datasets easier to analyze for research questions involving survival, treatment, biomarkers, and patient characteristics.
method: Uses a ReAct-style LLM agent to select among 8 tools for extraction, statistics, survival analysis, hypothesis testing, and verification.
Cross-checks outputs against the curated TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource (CDR) and provides source-attributed, traceable results.
Evaluated on TCGA-Agent-Bench with 440 queries spanning five difficulty tiers.
evidence_signal: The system reached 93.4% overall accuracy, outperforming a rule-based pipeline, single-pass LLM, and retrieval-augmented generation; it was especially strong on fields missing from the CDR, answering 100% of 26 targeted queries versus 3.8% for CDR-only.
watch_item: Performance depends on tool design and data coverage, so results may be weaker when clinical fields are missing, ambiguous, or require careful validation.
paper_title: A ReAct Agentic AI System for Natural Language Querying and Statistical Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas Clinical Data
